aspects.says: A decorator and a proxy keep the interface they wrap; an adapter changes it and adds nothing.
basis: section:Java Has Only Object Adapters When the Target Is a Class
aspects.reason: a one-clause pointer to units 9.2.2 and 9.2.3, whose practices check decorators and proxies

aspects.says: A receiver that must not see the array's changes, or make its own, gets a copy: new ArrayList<>(...) or List.copyOf(...).
basis: section:Arrays.asList Adapts an Array Without Copying It, So Sorting the List Reorders the Array

aspects.says: Arrays.asList copies nothing: the list reads and writes the array, so sorting or setting through the list changes the array, and changes to the array show in the list.
basis: section:Arrays.asList Adapts an Array Without Copying It, So Sorting the List Reorders the Array

aspects.says: Arrays.asList adapts arrays of objects only: given an int[] it returns a one-element List<int[]>, and the JDK has no List<Integer> view of an int[].
basis: section:Arrays.asList Adapts an Array Without Copying It, So Sorting the List Reorders the Array

aspects.says: A CompletableFuture made with new completes only when code completes it, so a callback adapter that ignores the legacy API's failure callback leaves its callers waiting forever.
basis: section:A Callback Adapter Must Complete the Future on Every Path the Legacy Call Can Take

aspects.says: InputStreamReader built with a Charset replaces malformed input with U+FFFD; built with a decoder from newDecoder() it throws MalformedInputException.
basis: section:InputStreamReader Adapts Bytes to Chars Through a Charset, and the One-Argument Constructor Takes the JVM's Default

aspects.says: InputStreamReader without a charset decodes with the JVM's default charset, which a start option can change, so the same bytes read correctly on one machine and garbled, without an error, on another.
basis: section:InputStreamReader Adapts Bytes to Chars Through a Charset, and the One-Argument Constructor Takes the JVM's Default

aspects.says: When the target is a class, such as Reader, a class adapter doesn't compile and only an object adapter works; for an interface target a class adapter still adapts only instances it constructs.
basis: section:Java Has Only Object Adapters When the Target Is a Class

aspects.says: InputStreamReader keeps the bytes of an unfinished character until the next read completes it; decoding each read on its own turns a split multi-byte character into replacement characters.
basis: section:InputStreamReader Adapts Bytes to Chars Through a Charset, and the One-Argument Constructor Takes the JVM's Default

aspects.says: A non-async stage attached before the future completes runs on the thread that completes it, here the legacy client's I/O thread; slow work goes to thenApplyAsync with an executor.
basis: section:Continuations Run on Whichever Thread Completes the Future

aspects.says: An exception the legacy call throws on the caller's thread must become a failed future; otherwise it leaves the adapter past the caller's exceptionally.
basis: section:A Callback Adapter Must Complete the Future on Every Path the Legacy Call Can Take
